away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. away.headline: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. Ready to Step Into Familiar but Uncharted Territory
away.blurb: “It’s exciting,” Penix told reporters Wednesday. “I imagine I should have a lot of people coming to the game. My mom usually knows that headcount. But it’s going to be exciting to be able to get out there.” “His very first steps as a baby – they were actually in the end zone,’’ Penix, Sr. told Tom Brew. “His first steps were right out there on the football field, right there in the end zone with me. How’s that for a start?’’ As a rookie, Penix was backing up Kirk Cousins before taking over as the starter for the final three games of the 2024 season in what was planned to be a redshirt year. Last year, when the Falcons made the trip to Tampa, Penix had already torn his ACL and was ruled out for the season less than a month earlier. “It’s happening,” Penix said of finally playing near his Central Florida home. “Can’t wait to be out there. We want to come out with a win.” “You practice it, you look over all the looks that they’ve brought, you go years back, and just be ready for everything,” Penix detailed the preparation. “We try to make sure we don’t miss any pressure looks that we possibly can see. And every week, a team comes in with a new pressure. And once we figure that out, we make adjustments on the sideline or at halftime. We’ll be ready.” Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. Ready to Step Into Familiar but Uncharted Territory Skip to main content SI.COM Third-year NFL quarterback Michael Penix Jr. now has a season’s worth of starts at 17. But there’s one thing the Atlanta Falcons signal-caller hasn’t done yet. This Sunday, Penix will be about 40 miles north of his hometown, Dade City, when Atlanta (3-4) heads to Raymond James Stadium for a Week 8 NFC South road clash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) . Penix was originally born in Cookeville, Tennessee, where his father, Michael Sr., starred as a running back and his mother, Takisha, was a track and field athlete at Tennessee Tech. The family then relocated to Dade City and later to Riverview. In a 2019 interview with Indiana Hoosiers on SI , Penix Sr. shared that his baby, Penix Jr., took his first steps in the end zone of a local football field. Penix played prep football at Pasco High School and then finished his final two years at Tampa Bay Technical High School. He hasn’t played a game at home since. Before transferring to finish his college career at the University of Washington, Penix’s Hoosiers team played in the 2021 Outback Bowl, hosted by Raymond James Stadium. The quarterback watched from the sidelines with a torn ACL, the second of three in his football career. Penix has faced the Bucs before, though, in the 2025 season opener. Atlanta hosted, but dropped the game 23-20. The quarterback went 27-for-42 for 298 passing yards and threw a touchdown. Now 26, Penix was two years old when the Bucs won their first Super Bowl in January 2003 to cap off the 2002-2003 season. But he added he was never a fan of the team growing up. home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. home.headline: Buccaneers’ Emeka Egbuka among players included in latest injury report before Falcons game
home.blurb: Egbuka was a limited participant in Thursday's practice as he continued to work through the NFL's concussion protocol. One encouraging sign was his return to a regular practice jersey after previously wearing a non-contact one. The development suggests he is making progress, though he still needs medical clearance before returning to game action. The rookie has been out since sustaining a concussion and a foot injury in the Buccaneers' Week 6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers . During the fourth quarter, Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen delivered a hit that brought his shoulder into Egbuka's helmet as the receiver tried to make a play on an incomplete pass. The injuries forced him to sit out Tampa Bay's Week 7 win over the Carolina Panthers. His return would give the Buccaneers another important option in their passing game. Before going down, Egbuka had caught 28 passes for 240 yards and two touchdowns, making him a productive contributor to the team's receiving corps. Luke Goedeke missed Thursday's practice with a calf injury, while Kenny Gainwell was limited by a hip issue. Yaya Diaby and Josiah Trotter returned to full participation, as did Baker Mayfield and Antoine Winfield Jr. The Buccaneers will have to wait and see how Egbuka responds as they prepare to host Atlanta at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday. His return to a regular practice jersey is a positive step, but he must still progress through the concussion protocol and receive final medical clearance to suit up on Sunday. However, Egbuka's recovery from both the concussion and foot injury will ultimately determine whether he can return against Atlanta. Thomas has averaged nearly 18.5 yards per catch against the Colts in his career, and this could be another day of big plays. picks.headline: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8
picks.blurb: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8 Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars didn't play in Week 7, they managed to gain ground in the AFC South , as every other team in the division lost. The Jags are back from their break and will have a prime opportunity to keep building their lead when they play the hapless Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Colts are 2-5 and currently showing no signs of getting better this season. Heck, they let everyone know that they're punting on the season when they ousted general manager Chris Ballard, who failed to replenish the Indianapolis roster and left it devoid of talent. Following the dismissal of Ballard, Indy has gone on to hold a fire sale, sending All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in return for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth in 2028 days before the Jaguars game. While the Nelson trade could incentivize the Jags to make a push for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , they cannot lose sight of the task at hand, which is beating the dreaded divisional foe. And with this in mind, here are the early odds for Week 8 and a bold Parker Washington prediction. The Colts vs. the Jaguars early odds for Week 8 The game will be held at EverBank Stadium, where the Colts have lost 11 consecutive games. Not surprisingly, the Jaguars are a 7.5-point favorite with a moneyline of -395 , via DraftKings. Bet $395 on them to win $100 if they beat Indianapolis for a total payout of $495. The Colts' moneyline sits at +310. Place a wager of $100 and win $310 if they beat Jacksonville for a total payout of $410. The over/under for the game is set at 49.5 points. ** Keep in mind that odds are refreshed periodically, so they can change at any moment. You may also like: 5 Jaguars who need to step up after the bye Bold Parker Washington prediction for the Jaguars vs. the Colts One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Jaguars in the offseason was that they opted not to make a big splash in free agency because they wanted to take care of their homegrown talent. Thus far, they locked up long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Travon Walker, cornerback Montaric Brown, and tight end Brenton Strange, so you could make the case that general manager James Gladstone achieved the goal. That said, Parker Washington is still waiting on an extension. A sixth-round pick in 2023, Washington showed flashed his first two seasons but was stucked behind Christian Kirk. Jacksonville paved the way for him to start when Kirk was traded to the Houston Texans. Right off the bat, Washington became a key contributor on offense, registering 58 receptions for 807 yards with five touchdowns, all career bests, last year. Washington wasted no time picking up where he left off last year, racking up 26 receptions for 416 yards with four touchdowns. The former Penn State Nittany Lion is on pace to register the first 1,000-yard season of his career and should have no trouble getting the top-market contract he's been looking for . Although the Jags reportedly offered Washington $25 million per year before Week 1 , he rejected the offer. It's possible that he's aiming for an annual average of $30 million. Based on his production, he may be able to get it, and he'll have a prime opportunity when he plays the Colts. Already, Washington posted his first 100-yard game of the season against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. He'll get his second one in Week 8 when he registers seven receptions for a monster 140 yards with two touchdowns against Indy. INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts have made a flurry of roster moves this week, trying to cover a rash of injuries at the cornerback position while shoring up depth at linebacker. Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen was a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day after missing last week’s game due to an ankle injury, although his fellow rookie, Bryce Boettcher, missed his second consecutive day with a groin injury. Indianapolis feels confident enough in its linebacker group to release veteran Germaine Pratt, who was signed to the practice squad two weeks ago but no longer has a path to playing time. Pratt played 20 snaps against Minnesota this week due to injuries, but the Colts plan to move Allen into the starting lineup now that he’s healthy. Pratt was a starter for 12 games in Indianapolis in 2025; the Colts are trying to get younger and faster at the position. “C.J. was going to start this week before he had that injury,” defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said. “I think they’re all putting their time in, and the more at bats they get, the better they’re going to be.” The Colts have larger issues at cornerback. Sauce Gardner practiced in full for the first time since suffering a calf injury against Tennessee, offering a potential starting option. Indianapolis placed Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve earlier this week, and Justin Walley missed the second consecutive day with a knee injury. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, only Jordan Mason has an injury designation, but his questionable designation is a technical one for those coming off of IR. He will play on Sunday. Christian Darrisaw and Harrison Smith had their customary rest days on Friday. For the Colts, a total of seven players have injury designations. The most significant are starting cornerback Sauce Gardner and starting tight end Tyler Warren, both of whom are out, as is wide receiver Anthony Gould. Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher is questionable, as is his backup C.J. Allen, which could leave them thin at the position. The same is true at cornerback with Sauce Gardner out and Justin Walley questionable. Lastly, punter Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice all week and is listed as questionable. The Colts added a punter to their roster this week in case he can’t go on Sunday. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. Los Angeles Rams have no clear date for Myles Garrett's return McVay has yet to decide whether the Rams will open Garrett's 21-day practice window, which would allow the defensive end to begin working toward a return. Speaking to reporters on October 26, the coach said he needed to consult the team's medical staff before making that call. Early reports suggested he might return after four weeks, but the recovery period later stretched to six weeks or longer. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last week that Garrett was likely to return to practice, with a possible Week 8 appearance in the discussion. Opening the practice window would not guarantee an immediate return to games. The Rams would have 21 days to activate Garrett to the 53-man roster or place him on season-ending injured reserve. Until the team makes that move, he cannot play. Other reports have suggested the wait could continue. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported on October 21 that Garrett was likely to miss at least another two or three weeks. That timeline could push his return toward Week 10, with the Rams scheduled to have a bye in Week 11. Los Angeles improved to 3-4 after beating the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, but the team has little room for further setbacks. home.headline: Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams
home.blurb: Myles Garrett has not played for the Los Angeles Rams since Week 1 and the team still is not sure if the edge rusher will return to the field any time soon. Sean McVay was asked about Garrett returning for the Los Angeles Chargers game on Sunday, and the head coach said that he wasn't sure if L.A.'s superstar offseason acquisition would practice this week or not. McVay was asked about both Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson potentially making a return to practice this week, but answered that he wasn't prepared to answer yet. The longer Garrett doesn't suit up, the harder it will be for the Rams to stay afloat in a tough 2026 season where the Rams need to go on a run to make Garrett's return worth it from a playoff perspective. By the time Garrett is ready, if he's ready, will there be a point to playing this season? Or, will it better to wait for 2027? Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams Danny Stone Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:41 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads McVay said he needs to meet with Reggie Scott, the Rams' Senior Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance, before he makes any type of determination. "I'm not sure yet. I'm not decided on those things." A follow-up question was asked with regard to when McVay would know whether or not either player would practice this week. McVay only offers further that he'll meet with the medical team and go from there. McVay doesn't offer any insight to how he thinks that meeting will go, just that he needs to meet with them before making a decision. "Once I get with Reggie and talk about the approach for the week. Then we'll just kinda follow their guidance based on where he's at and how he's feeling." It could be gamesmanship, it could be McVay wanted to have genuine deniability for this presser about whether Garrett will play this week or not, but at some point the team will need to make a decision on Garrett. And hopefully soon because the team invested a lot into him as an addition for a defense that is lacking serious firepower upfront this season. The Rams traded a first-round pick, Jared Verse, and more to to get Garrett . He hasn't played in a game since Week 1, as the 2025 sack leader has yet to notch one single sack or tackle for his new team. As McVay might say, "I'm not sure yet. I'm not decided on those things."

home.headline: Myles Garrett injury update, timeline from Rams coach raises eyebrows
home.blurb: Despite growing optimism last week that superstar defensive end Myles Garrett was nearing a return, Rams head coach Sean McVay poured cold water on those expectations Wednesday, announcing that neither Garrett nor tight end Terrance Ferguson will have their 21-day practice windows opened this week. The news comes less than a week after NFL insider Ian Rapoport suggested Garrett could return to practice this week. Those expectations now appear premature. "So whatever reports are out there, make sure they're accurate," McVay said. Under NFL rules, players placed on injured reserve must miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. Garrett satisfied that requirement following the Rams' Week 5 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, but Los Angeles has yet to open his practice window. With McVay ruling out a practice return this week, Garrett's earliest possible game appearance is now Week 9 against the Washington Commanders in the nation's capital. "We don't talk too much about our jobs per se, and our sports. I think that's like a really fun thing about our relationship," Kim said. "But the thing about Myles and everyone who knows him is this he is such a hard worker and he is doing everything he can to get back out there. Doing everything he can to get back stronger and he's well on his way. The thing about that man is he is stubborn in the best ways, and no injury is going to hold him back." Los Angeles entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations, only to watch injuries steadily strip away important pieces of its roster, as the team got out to a 2-4 start to the season. Garrett was supposed to be a centerpiece of a revamped defense capable of terrorizing opposing quarterbacks. picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Bet on the Chicago Bears to cover the spread on Monday night at sportsbooks On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes wild. It should be a good game, and if that holds true it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

picks.headline: Broncos vs Chiefs preview: Denver attempts a redo
picks.blurb: Broncos vs Chiefs preview: Denver attempts a redo - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin Broncos vs Chiefs preview: Denver attempts a redo KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a play against the Kansas City Chiefs during the second half of an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The first game of the 2026 season for your Denver Broncos did not go according to plan. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Kansas City : Sixth in total offense (380.5 yards per game), fifth in rushing offense (141.5 YPG), 11th in passing offense (239.0 YPG), 14th in scoring offense (23.8 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (270.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing offense (94.9 YPG), 27th in passing offense (175.1 YPG), tied for 24th in scoring offense (20.6 points per game). Defensive Rankings Kansas City : Fourteenth in total defense (323.3 yards per game), 13th in rushing defense (99.5 YPG), 17th in passing defense (223.8 YPG), second in scoring defense (17.2 points per game). Denver : Twenty-third in total defense (349.0 yards per game), 28th in rushing defense (133.3 YPG), 12th in passing defense (215.7 YPG), seventh in scoring defense (20.1 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Win the turnover battle on Sunday, and the Broncos put themselves in a great spot to win the game. — Ian St. Clair Stop the Chiefs run game Mahomes is continuing to play based off who he was two years ago and not putting in the effort to stay great. I like our chances if we force him to throw on our excellent secondary. Stop Kenneth Walker and win the game. — Sadaraine Tackle Kenneth Walker III The Broncos were hanging tough in the first half in that Week 1 matchup, but the horrific tackling eventually led to big plays in the run game. The Chiefs ran away from Denver in the second half. We all remember how much we overreacted to that first game, but man, did they miss too many tackles to count, and the overreaction was warranted. Since then, however, the Broncos defense has been pretty damn good and the offense is finally waking up. Keep up that momentum, and they should take care of business this weekend. — Tim Lynch Feed Jonah Coleman No need to get cute. Let Jonah Coleman build off the game he had against the Arizona Cardinals. Commit to the running attack. Get the young guys involved. Coleman and RJ Harvey had great games in Phoenix. Keep that going. The passing attack will open up once teams are forced to respect the run. — Adam Malnati Score more points than KC Using advanced analytics, the keys to this game are simple. When the Broncos score fewer points than their opponent, they are 0-2, and when they score more, they are 5-0. Further proving this point, they are 0-1 vs. the Chiefs this season when scoring fewer points than them. However, they were 2-0 against the Chiefs last season when they scored more points than their division rivals. So, according to these advanced analytics, if they can score more points than the Chiefs in this game, they will be 6-2. — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown Photo by: Joe Camporeale Stephan Stroud Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:28 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs will travel to Denver on Sunday for a crucial AFC West matchup against the Broncos. With Kansas City sitting at 5-1 and Denver at 5-2, both teams have plenty at stake as they look to strengthen their position in the division race. The game is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High and will air on CBS. The Broncos enter with momentum after winning three consecutive games, while the Chiefs are looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season. Chiefs Look to Bounce Back Head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes will try to get Kansas City back on track after a disappointing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs struggled to generate offense, finishing with just 213 total yards and failing to reach the red zone. Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception in the defeat. He will need a stronger performance against a Denver defense that has consistently pressured opposing quarterbacks this season. Running back Kenneth Walker III could be a major factor after dominating the Broncos in the teams' first meeting. Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City's 31-10 victory in September. If the Chiefs can establish their ground game again, it could open opportunities for Mahomes and the passing attack. Broncos Aim to Protect Home Field Denver head coach Sean Payton will look to keep his team's winning streak alive behind quarterback Bo Nix. The second-year quarterback has shown his ability to make plays with both his arm and legs, and he delivered an impressive performance in the Broncos' 30-16 win over Arizona. Nix threw for 222 yards and added 73 rushing yards, including a 62 yard touchdown run. His mobility could be important against a Kansas City defense that will try to disrupt Denver's offensive rhythm. The Broncos' defense will also be key. Led by pass rushers Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, Denver has the ability to pressure Mahomes and force mistakes. Cornerback Pat Surtain II's improved injury status could provide a boost to the secondary, although Denver's final injury report will be worth monitoring. What to Watch For The biggest matchup will be Kansas City's offense against Denver's pass rush. If the Broncos consistently pressure Mahomes, they could make life difficult for the Chiefs. However, Kansas City's experience and offensive talent make the visitors dangerous in any close game.

Tucker is considered to be one of the greatest kickers in NFL history, which makes sense considering he's made 89.1% of his field goal attempts. His time with the Ravens ultimately came to an end after he was accused of inappropriate behavior during massage sessions. The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists made accusations against Tucker, with two of the massage parlors claiming they banned him because of his behavior. "I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists." Tucker has conducted workouts with the Colts, Jets and Saints over the past two years. It wasn't until this Wednesday, however, that he landed a deal. According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star, the Chiefs are signing Tucker to their practice squad. If Tucker outperforms Butker at practice, he could end up starting as early as this Sunday against the Broncos.

home.headline: Broncos' first injury report for Week 8 paints an early bleak picture
home.blurb: Of note, Patrick Surtain II pracitced in full, so the Broncos should get him back, but all of Allen, Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga did not practice: The initial report with Waddle was that he aggravated his chest injury, but that there is 'hope' he can play on Sunday. Hufanga has already missed a couple of games due to his ankle injury, and if he does not practice in some capacity on Thursday, his status for Week 8 is in doubt. Allen has a hamstring injury and did not practice, either. The weird thing is that there was not any sort of report that came out with Allen's injury like we saw with Waddle, so that could end up being good news that it's pretty minor. We're definitely not going to make any declarations here since it's early in the week, but the Thursday statuses are going to be huge, as if any of the three "DNP" players from Wednesday are limited or full on Thursday, their chances of playing go way up. Sean Payton hilariously called himself out for awful Jaylen Waddle play call The Denver Broncos have consistently been among the healthiest teams in the NFL since Sean Payton took over back in 2023. That doesn't mean, though, the team has not dealt with injuries. Every NFL team has to deal with injuries in some capacity, and the teams that are usually standing in the end have better depth or better roster health overall. In Week 7, a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Broncos saw two key players leave the game in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and defensive end Zach Allen. And in the team's first injury report of Week 8, we see some key players on the report, and while it is early, their statuses for Week 8 could already be in doubt. Denver Broncos injury report is getting longer as Week 8 approaches However, if any of them again do not practice on Thursday, it would logically be unlikely that they play on Sunday. While the Broncos are more talented than Kansas City and get this game at home, not having even one of these players is going to be brutal. In the same way that 2025's home game against the Chiefs was important, this one is as well. The Broncos would be in first place in the AFC West with a win, but if they lose, the Chiefs would improve to 6-1, and Denver would drop to 5-3 with two losses to the Chiefs already etched into their record. It would severely hurt their chances at repeating as division champions. And as it concerns the pasing game, if the Broncos hope to build on their breakout from Week 7, having Waddle in the lineup would allow that to continue to happen. picks.blurb: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New England Patriots (4-3) head to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday looking to strengthen their position in the AFC playoff race against a Miami Dolphins (1-5) team that earned its first win of the season last week. The Patriots average 22.9 points per game compared with Miami’s 16.3. New England’s three-game winning streak ended in a 30-24 loss at Chicago last Thursday, despite Drake Maye completing 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a score. The loss can be attributed to a costly interception from Maye in the red zone in the second quarter and New England compounded it with 10 penalties and a defense that missed 16 tackles. Miami, meanwhile, is coming off its best afternoon of the season, a 28-25 road victory over the Jets on October 25 that gave coach Jeff Hafley his first win and kept the Dolphins from starting 0-6. Malik Willis was the catalyst, completing 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns to rookie Caleb Douglas , adding 37 rushing yards and another score, and converting a game-clinching fourth-and-1 in the final two minutes. Miami scored touchdowns on three of its first four possessions and led 21-7 at halftime before a late Jets comeback made things interesting. Ollie Gordon II rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown, while Douglas’ 63-yard fourth-quarter catch-and-run provided the winning points. This rivalry has swung toward New England recently after several seasons in which Miami consistently gave the Patriots problems. The teams’ most recent meeting came January 4, 2026, when New England completed a season sweep with a dominant 38-10 victory at Gillette Stadium to finish the 2025 regular season 14-3. Rhamondre Stevenson was the centerpiece, rushing seven times for 131 yards and two touchdowns and catching another touchdown from Maye, while TreVeyon Henderson added two rushing scores; Maye finished 14 of 18 for 191 yards and a touchdown before exiting early in the fourth quarter. New England outgained Miami 457-180. That capped the Patriots’ first season sweep of Miami since 2016. New England Patriots Media Relations WEEK 8 · Sun 11/01 · 4:25 PM EST New England Patriots Miami Dolphins PATRIOTS: Game Release (PDF) | Roster | Depth Chart | Stats DOLPHINS: Roster | Depth Chart | Stats | Roster Flip Card (PDF) The New England Patriots will be on the road for the second straight week when they travel to face the Miami Dolphins in the first of two 2026 meetings. The Dolphins will play at Gillette Stadium in the second game to close out the 2026 regular season. The date and time for that game have not been announced yet. Last season, the Patriots swept the series with a 33-27 win at Miami (9/14) and a 38-10 win to close out the 2025 regular season at Gillette Stadium (1/4). The Patriots will look to win their third straight game over the Dolphins and go 3-0 in the AFC East. Related Links How to Watch and Stream Sunday's Patriots Game Against the Dolphins | NFL Week 8 SERIES HISTORY The New England Patriots earned their 11th series sweep and first since the 2016 season last year with a 33-27 win at Miami (9/14) and a 38-10 win in the rematch in the final game of the season (1/4). The Patriots and Dolphins will meet for the second time in 2026 in the regular season finale at Gillette Stadium in a game that is not scheduled at this time. It will be the 19th time that the two teams will square off in the final game of the year and the second straight year that the Patriots will host the game. Nine of those final games have been played in New England with the Patriots holding a 5-4 edge in those games. Overall, the Patriots are 9-8 when facing Miami in the final game of the year. New England has the advantage against Miami in home games, leading the series 39-21 - including 18-6 at Gillette Stadium - but are 18-43 when playing on the road against Miami. The Dolphins and Patriots met for the first time in 1966 and began playing twice a year during the 1967 regular season, except in 1982 during a players' strike. The two teams have played three times in the postseason with New England holding a 2-1 advantage. Photo by Eric J. Adler SERIES BREAKDOWN MIAMI 64, NEW ENGLAND 57 (Including New England 2, Miami 1 in Playoffs) Record in New England: 39-21 (Incl. 1-0 in playoffs) Record in Foxborough: 37-19 (1-0) Gillette Stadium: 18-6 Record in Boston: 2-2 Record in Miami: 18-43 (Incl. 1-1 in playoffs) Record at Dolphins / Hard Rock: 14-25 Record at Orange Bowl: 3-18 (1-1) Record in Tampa: * 1-0 Season Sweeps: Patriots 11, Dolphins 16 Season Splits: 31 (Most recent 2022) *A Miami home game was played in Tampa in 1969. Since 2000, the Patriots are 113-49 (.698) against AFC East opponents. New England is 29-23 against the Dolphins over that span, 41- 12 against the New York Jets and 40-13 against the Buffalo Bills. The Patriots were 3-1 against Indianapolis from 2000 through 2001 when they were in the AFC East. 2026 REGULAR SEASON Divisional Standings Total Yards Gained Total Offense (Rank) Points Per Game Total Yards Allowed Total Defense (Rank) Points Allowed / Game Possession Avg. WHAT TO LOOK FOR A Patriots win would extend their streak to three straight wins against the Dolphins following their series sweep of Miami last season, their 11th between the division rivals. A Patriots win would give them a 3-0 record against AFC East opponents after a 29-26 win at Buffalo on Oct. 4 and a 26-19 win vs. the New York Jets on Oct. 18. In 2025, the Patriots started the year with a 3-0 record in the division. The Patriots scored more than 30 points in both wins against Miami last year with a 33-27 win at Miami on Sept. 14 and a 38-10 win at Gillette Stadium on Jan. 4, 2026. The Patriots have scored 30 points or more in both games against Miami six total times (1967, 1986, 2010, 2016, 2018 and 2025). PATRIOTS TO WATCH Weight: 249 lbs College: Arkansas TE Hunter Henry enters this week tied with Russ Francis with 28 touchdowns and needs 1 to move into sole possession of third place on the team's all-time list for touchdowns among tight ends. Rhamondre Stevenson Weight: 227 lbs College: Oklahoma RB Rhamondre Stevenson joined Jim Nance (45), Sam Cunningham (43), Corey Dillon (37), Steve Grogan (35), LeGarrette Blount (34), Tony Collins (32) and Curtis Martin (32) as the only Patriots players with 30 career rushing touchdowns after he scored on a 5-yard run in the first quarter against Las Vegas. He needs 2 rushing touchdowns to tie Curtis Martin and Tony Collins for sixth place on the Patriots alltime list for rushing touchdowns. He has had 2 rushing touchdowns in a game six times, with the last coming in the 2025 season-finale vs. Miami on Jan. 4, 2026. Stevenson has 206 career receptions and joined Kevin Faulk (431), James White (381), Tony Collins (261) and Sam Cunningham (210) as the only New England running backs with 200 receptions. He needs 4 receptions to tie Sam Cunningham for fourth place among all Patriots running backs in career receptions. Stevenson (3,954) needs 46 yards to join Sam Cunningham (5,453), Jim Nance (5,323) and Tony Collins (4,647) as the only Patriots players to reach 4,000 rushing yards. Stevenson had a career-high 93 yards receiving last week at Chicago. If he registers at least 90 yards receiving this week, he will become just the second Patriots running back with back-to-back games with at least 90 yards receiving. RB Ron Burton had 94 yards receiving at Houston on Nov. 18, 1962 and followed that performance with 97 yards receiving on Nov. 23, 1962 vs. Buffalo. Stevenson enters this week in 22nd place on the Patriots all-time scoring list with 220 points. With a touchdown this week at Miami, he will move ahead of Wes Welker (225) and tie Curtis Martin (226) for 20th on the team's all-time list. Weight: 225 lbs College: North Carolina QB Drake Maye completed a 48-yard touchdown pass to RB Rhamondre Stevenson at the end of the second quarter last week at Chicago for his 11th touchdown of at least 30 yards over the last two seasons. He then threw a 30-yard touchdown pass to TE Eli Raridon in the third quarter for his 12th, the most in the NFL over that span. Josh Allen and Jalen Hurts each have nine touchdowns of at least 30 yards over the last two seasons. It is Maye's second 40-yard touchdown pass of the 2026 season. He had a 42-yard touchdown pass to WR Romeo Doubs vs. the New York Jets on Oct. 18, 2026. Maye has had two games this year with 2 touchdown passes of at least 30 yards. In addition to the two at Chicago, he also had a 35- yard touchdown pass to WR DeMario Douglas and a 34-yard touchdown pass to WR Kyle Williams in the win vs. Las Vegas on Oct. 11, 2026. He also had two 30-yard touchdown passes on Oct. 13, 2024 vs. Houston with a 40-yard touchdown pass and 35-yard touchdown pass. If Maye has one more game this season with at least two 30- yard touchdown passes, he will match the team record for the most games with at least two 30-yard touchdown passes in a game with three such games, set by Steve Grogan (1979 and 1983) and Tom Brady (2007 and 2009). If Maye throws 2 touchdowns of at least 30 yards this week at Miami, he will join Tom Brady (2009 - Oct. 18 vs. Tennessee and Oct. 25 at Tampa Bay; 2007 - Oct. 14 at Dallas and Oct. 21 at Miami) and Mike Taliaferro (1969 - Nov. 23 vs. Buffalo and Nov. 30 at Miami) as the only Patriots quarterbacks to throw two 30-yard touchdown passes in consecutive games. Maye has gone four straight games with at least 2 touchdown passes. Maye had a streak of five straight games with at least 2 touchdown passes last season. The Patriots record for most consecutive games in a season with at least 2 touchdown passes is 10 by Tom Brady in 2007 and 2014. Maye threw for 321 yards last week against Chicago. If he throws for 300 yards this week against Miami, he will be the first Patriots quarterback with back-to-back 300-yard games since Tom Brady in 2019 when he threw for 348 yards at Washington (10/6) and 334 yards vs. the New York Giants (10/10). Christian Elliss Weight: 231 lbs College: Idaho LB Christian Elliss tied a career-high with 13 total tackles last week at Chicago. He also had 13 total tackles vs. Buffalo on Jan. 5, 2025. The last Patriots player to reach 10 or more tackles in back-to-back games was LB Robert Spillane in 2025 with 15 tackles vs. Pittsburgh (9/21) and 10 vs. Carolina (9/28). Darius Muasau Weight: 230 lbs College: UCLA LB Darius Muasau leads the team with 8 special teams tackles and needs 2 this week to reach 10 total special teams tackles. Last season, the Patriots had four players reach double digit special teams tackles with LB Christian Elliss (18), S Brenden Schooler (14), LB Marte Mapu (12) and LB Jack Gibbens (10). Muasau has three games in 2026 with 2 special teams tackles: at Buffalo (10/4), vs. Las Vegas (10/11) and at Chicago (10/22). Since 2000, the team record for the most games with at least 2 special teams tackles is eight games by LB Larry Izzo in 2004. away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. For the Patriots, especially considering that they were on a short week, this is definitive good news. The team, after all, had at least lost some starters or key reserves to injury in almost every game this season so far. Now heading into a Week 8 contest against the Miami Dolphins off a mini-bye, they seemingly are trending in the right direction again. No major injuries were added on Thursday, while the team is getting healthier — as evidenced by the fact that guard Ben Brown (knee) also was back on the practice fields on Monday. away.headline: A.J. Brown injury update: Patriots WR misses practice with knee issue, status for Sunday 'up in the air'
A.J. Brown injury update: Patriots wide receiver misses more practice
away.blurb: Brown did not practice with the rest of his team on Thursday, Oct. 29, according to multiple reports. The star wide receiver was already limited in practice on Wednesday, Oct. 28 with a couple of lower body injuries, but his practice status has regressed as the week has progressed. The former Philadelphia Eagles wideout has already missed four games this season after a high ankle sprain in Week 1 landed him on injured reserve . Brown has played in three out of the Patriots ' seven games since New England sent a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick to Philadelphia to acquire the receiver . The 29-year-old Brown did not practice on Oct. 29 as he deals with injuries to his ankle and knee. NFL Media and ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported on Oct. 29 that the Patriots initially listed Brown on their injury report on Oct. 28 as a limited participant with a knee injury. The team has since added an ailing ankle to the receiver's injury designation as he misses practice for the first time since his Week 6 return. That is a notably short list of healthy receivers – and Brown may not be healthy. New England already has the other two of its top three receivers out on injured reserve: Romeo Doubs with a shoulder and Mack Hollins with a calf. The Patriots do have four more wide receivers on their practice squad to fill out their depth, especially if Brown is unable to play in Week 8: Ryan Miller, Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon and Chandler Brayboy. Brown 's comeback may have lasted all of two games. As a Week 8 clash with the Miami Dolphins approaches, Brown appears to be at risk of missing a fifth game this year. Here's what we know about the three-time Pro Bowler's status: Brown has appeared to be less than 100% recovered in his first two games back off of injured reserve. The wideout made his comeback in Week 6 against the Jets, where he promptly dropped two of his 10 targets and finished the game with just three catches. In Week 7 against the Bears, Brown caught three of his six targets but was 0-for-2 on contested targets and tallied just one yard after the catch, per Pro Football Focus. Brown's status for Week 8 remains unknown. Here's how things would look in the Patriots' receivers room if Brown is able to go on Sunday, Nov. 1: Miller is in his fourth season and appeared in five games for the Dolphins this year before they waived him. Dorner and Dixon are both UDFA rookies. Brayboy is a second-year receiver yet to make his NFL debut.

An illness kept Henderson out of Thursday's practice in Foxborough. The No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft stands with 203 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and one touchdown through 57 touches this fall for the backfield. He saw a season-low three carries during his most recent outing, however. Out wide, since being activated back to the 53-man roster after four games away, Brown has played 101 out of 122 offensive snaps. But the June trade acquisition stands with just six receptions for 75 yards through those recent starts. And now with a knee flare-up coming out of the team's mini bye. The rest of the active roster includes wide receivers DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. That's with veteran targets Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins both on injured reserve . Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee. The battle of the NFC East basement sees the Philadelphia Eagles visiting the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but Week 8 goes a long way to defining the second half of the schedule. My Eagles vs. Commanders predictions see SNF swinging in a different direction than the current markets would suggest, which is kind of on par with this upside-down division. Here are my favorite NFL picks for prime time on Nov. 1. TOP Pick Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with Dallas for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completions with two TDs in a loss to San Francisco on Oct. 19. Eagles vs Commanders combo There's a lot of big-name firepower missing on both sides, but I see more meat on the bone for these offenses – especially considering that the complementing stop units are both garbage. Washington allowed Dallas Goedert to find the end zone twice in Week 1 and have given up the second most TDs to tight ends heading into Week 8. With the Eagles' receiving corps running thin, Goedert's role spikes on SNF. Rookie WR Antonio Williams is filling the void left by Terry McLaurin, doing plenty of damage out of the slot. He burned Philly in his NFL debut and is projected for as many as 46 receiving yards in Week 8. Goedert drew seven targets for five receptions in Week 7 and has been McKee's safety blanket during his two-game stint as the starter. The Eagles face a Commanders defense that has been bullied by rival tight ends this season. Washington ranks dead last in DVOA vs. tight ends, allowing the seventh most yards to the position along with eight touchdowns to TEs in just six games. Goedert is responsible for two of those touchdowns, with a pair of scores in the win over Washington in Week 1. picks.blurb: Your next job? Just across the Delaware At 87, Sandra Folzer eyes another record Rutgers-Camden stages ‘No, No, Nanette’ IBX offers new plan options for 2027 News Politics Health Health News Children's Health Culture Food & Drink Entertainment Arts & Culture Events Festivals Expos & Conventions Family-Friendly Sports Eagles Fantasy Football Staff / Contributors Company Info About Us Legal / Privacy October 30, 2026 The Eagles have lost five straight, and Jayden Daniels hasn't won a start since last October. Jalen Carter will be looking for redemption after a bad night last week against Dallas. The Eagles are spiraling, and usually, the Commanders would present a break in the schedule. But this year is different. Injuries have piled up, some talent has even regressed, playcalling is inept, and so is much of the execution on the field. The Eagles are 2-5, the season is only slipping further away from them, and the Commanders this week on Sunday Night Football might not be the chance to stop the slide. Our picks and predictions for Week 8... • GAME INFO • Eagles (2-5) at Commanders (1-4-1) BROADCAST INFO BETTING LINES PHI +190 WSH -230 PHI +198 WSH -240 PHI +200 WSH -250 PHI +220 WSH -275 PHI +205 WSH -250 *Lines as of Thursday, Oct. 29 Jimmy Kempski (6-1) Commanders 24, Eagles 16 Jayden Daniels is 0-7-1 in his last eight starts. He is playing behind a bad offensive line and alongside some pretty unthreatening skill position players. The Commanders also have a very bad defense. And yet, they are definitively better than this Eagles team that has an offense with no answers and an extremely disappointing defense. The Eagles might be the worst team in the NFL right now, and I don't think that's some "hot take." MORE: Analyzing Nick Sirianni's job security as the Eagles' head coach Geoff Mosher (5-2) Commanders 26, Eagles 20 It's just hard to give the Eagles any benefit of the doubt right now. The Commanders have just one win, but they beat the defending Super Bowl champs and nearly beat the 4-win Giants before Jayden Daniels blew it at the end. They also came within a possession of the 49ers, and they're coming off their bye week. The Eagles will probably be doling out carries to Eli Mitchell and Jaydon Blue. Tanner McKee didn't take any opportunities to really drive the ball. The defense has been suspect all year. It's really a coin flip game, but the Eagles haven't won those kinds lately. Evan Macy (6-1) Commanders 23, Eagles 21 I want to pick the Eagles — they're bad but they're not 2-15 bad. They aren't going winless for the rest of the season. But with so much uncertainty as to who Tanner McKee will be throwing to, it might not be the week they end the losing streak . I think they're going to eventually find some kind of groove, string together some wins and bust their draft position. They'll win six or seven games. But they're not there yet. It will be a tough to watch tight loss in DC Sunday night. Nick Tricome (6-1) Commanders 24, Eagles 10 The Eagles aren't going to win. The offense is too banged up and spread thin, and with the way the defense checked out against Dallas last week, they're just a team that's spent and ready to pack it in. If the Commanders play them anywhere close to the way they did in Week 1, there's not going be anyhting to save the Eagles this time. Jalen Hurts isn't there now. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys. home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles opened their Week 8 preparations Wednesday with an extensive injury report, listing six players as nonparticipants and another six as limited participants ahead of Sunday's NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders . Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. home.blurb: • Unsurprisingly, Saquon Barkley was listed with a DNP after he struggled to stay on the field last Monday night against the Cowboys. • The Eagles are getting healthier on the edge, as Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, and Jonathan Greenard were all limited participants. • QB Jalen Hurts (IR, season over) : Hurts is out indefinitely with blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee has taken over as the team's starting quarterback. • RB Tank Bigsby (IR, eligible to return after Week 8) : Bigsby suffered an injury Week 4 against the Rams that required core muscle surgery. He will likely return this season, but could miss up to two months. • RB Will Shipley (IR, eligible to return after Week 9) : Shipley suffered a Lisfranc injury and will be out a while. Shipley is the Eagles' best RB in pass protection, but he only has 57 yards on 20 carries this season. • RB Dameon Pierce (IR, eligible to return after Week 12) : The Eagles' top four RBs are all injured. • The Commanders have a bunch of guys on injured reserve (below), but the only two names of note who did not practice on Wednesday were WR Stefon Diggs and DT Javon Kinlaw. • Stefon Diggs was a full participant after sitting out on Wednesday. • LT Laremy Tunsil (IR) : During training camp, Tunsil tore his triceps and will be out for a chunk of the regular season. He is arguably the best player on Commanders' roster. The Commanders didn't have much in the way of ideal replacements. They settled on Brandon Coleman, who was in a camp battle with Chris Paul for the starting LG spot. Coleman started 12 games for the Commanders at LT in 2024. He also started three games at LT when Tunsil got hurt last season. Massive downgrade. So far in 2026, PFF has Coleman down for 4 sacks allowed. • RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt : Croskey-Merritt is the Commanders' RB1. He had a good rookie season as a runner, carrying 175 times for 805 yards (4.6 YPC) and 8 TDs. However, he also had fumbling issues and was not a threat as a receiver. In 2026, he carried 67 times for 239 yards (3.6 YPC) and 2 TDs before landing on IR with a groin injury.
