The Chicago Bears and Caleb Williams are 5-2 and riding high off a primetime win in Week 7, but now they’ll have to go on the road to take on the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. Seattle also won in primetime in Week 7, holding the Kansas City Chiefs to just three points on Sunday Night Football to get back over .500 this season (4-3). These two teams are both in second place in their respective divisions, and this game could have massive wild card implications in the NFC. The NFC North currently has four teams over .500 while the NFC West has two with the 3-4 Los Angeles Rams lurking as a viable Super Bowl contender if they can get healthy. Oddsmakers have set the Seahawks as favorites in this game, and the opening odds tell us that they could end up being more than field-goal favorite by the time this game kicks off. Bears vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bears +3 (-102) Seahawks -3 (-118) Seahawks: -170 46.5 (Over -110/Under -110) Based on these odds (-170 on the moneyline), the Seahawks have an implied probability of 62.96 percent to win this game. Seattle is coming off a dominant defensive performance in Week 7, and it’s back at home where it is 3-1 so far in the 2026 season. However, the Bears have not lost a single game that Williams has started – and finished – this season. The Bears are an interesting team this season. A lot of their season-long offensive numbers are skewed a bit from the three games that Williams has missed, yet they’ve scored 30 or more points in every matchup that he’s been able to stay healthy in. Plus, Chicago is shockingly seventh in the league in success rate on defense despite allowing the most yards per play in the league. Oddsmakers are clearly buying the Seattle defense, which is No. 2 in EPA/Play, No. 2 in success rate and No. 1 in yards per play allowed – by a wide margin – this season. The Seahawks are allowing just 4.0 yards per play while the next-best team (Minnesota) is allowing 4.5. After the Seahawks shut down Patrick Mahomes in Week 7, it seems like oddsmakers have the defending champs’ defense as the best unit in this Week 8 clash. There’s a chance this line moves as the week progresses, and fans can look forward to Ben Johnson and Mike Macdonald scheming against each other in a potential playoff preview. A win for either team will go a long way because of tiebreakers with the NFC West and North featuring seven viable playoff teams. Only five will be able to get in (since the winners of the NFC East and NFC South will clinch two of the seven playoff spots). Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 8 Upset Pick Miami Dolphins (+250) vs. New England Patriots After getting three consecutive upset picks correct, I need to heat check myself. There’s no better way to do that than taking the one-win Dolphins against Drake Maye and the Patriots. Surprisingly, I have plenty of reasons to like this bet. Divisional games are often close, and New England has a long history of struggling in Miami. Also, the Dolphins have plenty of confidence after beating the Jets last week, and this offense is a lot better with rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas, who contributed two catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his first game since sustaining an ankle injury in Week 2. I’m playing with house money, and I’m putting it on the Dolphins. Peter Dewey Week 8 Upset Pick Atlanta Falcons (+114) vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Falcons may be the most confusing team in the NFL, but I think their best version is the top squad in the NFC South. I’m buying Atlanta as a road underdog against a Tampa Bay team that is 0-4 against the spread at home and potentially overvalued after a Week 7 rout of the Carolina Panthers. Baker Mayfield (thumb) wasn’t asked to do much, but the Bucs beat up a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the NFL. Plus, this Falcons offense has been much better with Michael Penix Jr. under center over the last few weeks. The Falcons are 3-2 when Penix starts, and I love this price against a Tampa Bay team with clear flaws and a quarterback at less than 100 percent. Iain MacMillan Week 8 Upset Pick Chicago Bears (+140) vs. Seattle Seahawks I'm ready to believe in the Chicago Bears. It did enough to beat the Chiefs last week, but their running game is still weak, and Sam Darnold hasn't been as efficient as he was a year ago. I'll take the Bears as my upset pick of the week. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sam Householder Thu, October 29, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Good teams play in big games and the Chicago Bears have a big game this week. They hit road to play the Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks. And they'll do it with a brand new All-Pro defensive tackle! Jeffery Simmons is a Bear! The Bears are proving themselves to be one of the best offenses in the league with one of the best rising-star quarterbacks. And their head coach and quarterback face a huge test against one of the league's best defenses. Chicago didn't fare so well in their first defensive test of the year, against the Minnesota Vikings. However, the weather was a factor in that game, like it or not. Plus, Caleb Williams didn't finish the game. Excuses, maybe, but also realities. This matchup has a lot of great storylines and will be a measuring stick for the Bears to see how they compete against the league's best. It feels like a game with playoff implications. It feels like a game worthy of the Monday Night Football spotlight. It will be the first game in November for the Bears, too. When teams really start to separate themselves. Let's meet the Seahawks. Seattle Seahawks SB Nation site : Field Gulls Record: 4-3, second in the NFC West Last week: 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs Game day, time, TV: Monday, 7:15 p.m. CT, ESPN Spread: Seattle -3.5 Bears all-time record against: 8-12, including 2-0 postseason Historical meeting: The Bears have never beaten the Seahawks in the month of November. In the second-ever meeting between the teams, the Seahawks beat the Bears 31-29 in week 10 of 1978. The Bears fell behind 21-9 with Jim Zorn hitting Steve Largent twice for touchdowns and Sherman Smith rushing for another. But Chicago made a strong comeback. Roland Harper scored on a 20-yard pass from Mike Phipps. After another Smith touchdown, Walter Payton scored from 7 yards out, drawing the Bears within six. The Seahawks drove down the field and tacked on another field goal to go up 31-22. Phipps threw a pick but Sam McCullum intercepted Zorn right back. Phipps put together a good drive and Harper scored a 2-yard TD with 40 seconds left. The Bears managed to recover the onside kick but with 12 seconds left, from Seattle's 46-yard line, Phipps' pass was intercepted to end the game. Last meeting: Who could forget the awful, terrible 6-3 Thursday Night Football game? Thomas Brown was coaching the Bears. It was a defensive slugfest. Or a total offensive mess. Depends on how you remember it. The most memorable play didn't count, as Caleb Williams rolled out and threw an off-platform pass to Rome Odunze four a touchdown. It was called back for offensive holding. (I cannot find a clip online, but I remember it was awesome). Offense: The Seahawks offense ranks 13th in points and 15th in yards. Their passing offense is 16th and their rushing offense ranks 17th. Sam Darnold (62.1 pct. cmp./1,290 yds./8 TD/8 INT) currently leads the league in interceptions, but played a lot better last week. Unless you've been living under a rock, you likely know about Jaxon Smith-Njigba (58 rec./867 yds./8 TD). Beyond him are AJ Barner (19/180/0), Cooper Kupp (18/199/1), deep threat Rashid Shaheed (16/163/0) and George Holani (12/88/0). Jadarian Price (28 att./119 yds./0 TD) is injured, but expected to return to practice this week along with Zach Charbonnett (no stats in 2026 yet). In their absence, it's been Emanuel Wilson (111 att./403 yds./3 TD) and Holani (26/108/1). Defense: Seattle's defense comes into Monday night as one the league's best. They rank fourth in points allowed and first in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks first in passing yards and sixth in rushing. The loaded unit stars Nick Emmanwori (27 tkls/3 TFL/2 sk/1 PD/7 QB hits), DTs Leonard Williams (3 sk/7 TFL/9 QB hits/1 PD), Byron Murphy (3 sk/ 24 tkls/5 TFL/6 QB hits) Derick Hall (3 sk/19 QB hits/3 TFL/1 FF/1 FR) and Ernest Jones (3 sk/68 tkls/3 TFL/2 QB hits/1 INT/3 PD) and Devon Witherspoon (41 tkls/3 PD/3 TFL/1 QB hits) Other playmakers are Julian Love (2 INT/6 PD/24 tkls/2 TFL), Nehemiah Pritchett (13 tkls/4 PD/2 INT) and Josh Jobe (27 tkls/1 PD/1 INT/1 TFL). Key matchups: This is a top offense against a top defense. The Bears are going to have to play disciplined football. Take what their given, take shots when they can, use play-action to suck in the LBs. On defense, stop JSN. That's no easy task. The Seahawks can find a running game if Price and/or Charbonnett are back. Anyway to get pressure on Sam Darnold is good though; we know what happens when he is pressured. The Seahawks haven't allowed a 300-yard passer this season. The Rams are the only team with more than 300 passing yards against Seattle since week 2 of last season. Seattle has lost only three times at home going back to the beginning of last season. The 49ers are the only team to beat Seattle at home during this span Despite their strong numbers, the Seahawks have allowed opponents to score on 78.6 percent of their trips inside of the red zone. The Seahawks' 13 offensive turnovers on the season rank fourth-most in the league. Their 12 defensive turnovers rank third-most. Seattle is allowing a league-low 144.4 passing yards per game and the second-worst passer rating of 72.6. Only the Vikings allow a worse QB rating Can the Bears hang with a team as good as the Seahawks? How will their offense and QB measure up against Seattle's defense?

picks.headline: Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears have demonstrated quite a bit of explosiveness this season, especially when Caleb Williams is under center and running back Kyle Monangai is healthy and in the lineup. Williams has been in the lineup for the past two games and has demonstrated no ill effects from the hamstring injury that sidelined him earlier in the year. Monangai has missed the last three games and while he is improving, there are no guarantees that he will be back in the lineup for this game. The Seahawks have not been at their best in the first half of the season and they take a 4-3 record into this home game. They are coming off a key Sunday night victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in which their defense performed at a peak level. They will need that kind of effort against the Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sam Darnold was one of the keys to Seattle's surge to last year's Super Bowl title. He has not been as efficient this season, as interceptions have been an issue. The Bears defense got a huge lift from their ability to create takeaways last year. They have not been as proficient in that area this season — minus-1 on the takeaway/turnover table — but they have been a middle-of-the-pack defense that has been moderately capable this season. This game could come down to turnover differential, and if the Bears are going to win on the road, they have to gain an advantage in this area. Williams will throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Williams has demonstrated that he can rise to the occasion and handle pressure. He has an excellent partnership with head coach Ben Johnson, and it appears that those two will allow the Bears to remain contenders in the division and the NFC for several years. Williams has all the tools that an outstanding quarterback needs, and as the No. 1 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, nearly all scouts and personnel specialists were predicting great things for him. However, Williams struggled in his rookie season under former head coach Matt Eberflus. That coach did not have the wherewithal to teach and demand outstanding play from Williams. However that changed under Johnson, and the quarterback reads and understands defenses, and he knows how to pick apart good defenses and make key plays. The one area that scouts did not get right about Williams was his speed and escapability from the pocket. He was thought to be above average or good in that area, and that assessment did not give him enough credit. He is sensational in that area. He has a strong partnership with wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as well as big-play tight end Colston Loveland. This trio should be able to cause problems for the Seattle defense, which is one of the strongest units in the league. Williams and the receivers will not overpower the Seahawks defense, but the quarterback will throw 2 TD passes and approach the 275-yard mark. Smith-Njigba is unstoppable, will exceed 125 yards and score a TD Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Bears regularly have to contend with outstanding receivers like Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson in the NFC North. However, Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is at another level. He is coming off a sensational game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Smith-Njigba was targeted 12 times by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold and he caught 9 passes for 150 yards and 1 touchdown. The Chiefs knew he was the central point of the Seattle offensive game plan, yet defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo could not do anything to slow him down. Stopping him was out of the question. Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will face the same issue. Allen certainly knows what it is like to face outstanding wideouts in the NFC North, but Smith-Njigba may be too strong for the Bears defense. He has caught 58 passes for 867 yards and 8 TDs, and asking CBs Jaylon Johnson, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon to prevent him from making big plays will be folly. The best way for the Bears to go about it would be pressuring Darnold and keep him from delivering accurate passes. The Bears have registered 19 sacks and Darnold has been trapped 14 times thus far. Allen's top priority will be to make sure his personnel gets in Darnold's face and prevents him from getting the ball to Smith-Njigba. That scenario is unlikely, but it is Chicago's best defensive hope. Bold game prediction: Seahawks 27, Bears 24 The Bears have the weapons to go into Seattle and give the defending champions a battle for 60 minutes. This is the kind of game that Johnson and Williams would like to use as a measuring stick. However, the Seahawks have already lost 3 games and they can't afford to lose any more. They will have a major challenge chasing down the 49ers in the NFC West, and dropping a home game to a solid team is not in their plans. The Seahawks played their best all-around game against the Chiefs in Week 7, and they will stay on track against the Bears. Seattle wins a close, well-played game against Williams and the Bears. away.headline: Seahawks-Bears Thursday injury report: Cross and Shaheed out, ‘Big Cat’ limited with Achilles
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks have a lengthy injury report to start their prep for the showdown with the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football with a whopping 18(!!) players listed with some sort of designation. The DNP’s for injury included Charles Cross, Rashid Shaheed, and Uchenna Nwosu. Notable limited participants were Tyrice Knight, Drake Thomas, the newly-returning Jadarian Price, and Leonard Williams who popped up with an Achilles injury…maybe I shouldn’t have used the word “popped” in his case. Find some wood to knock on if you’re superstitious. As this is the first injury report of the week, we’ll need to see how things shake out over the next few days to see who is really in danger of missing the primetime game. New Seahawks Quenton Nelson was listed as a full participant along with Zach Charbonnet. The hope is that both of them along with potentially Jadarian Price will help take the run game to another level, thus lessening the load on Sam Darnold’s shoulders. Mike Macdonald seemed relatively positive about Cross, saying that IR wasn’t in consideration at this time. The less time he misses, the more he’ll get to gel with his new partner in crime on the left side in Nelson.

away.headline: Bears QB Caleb Williams slapped with another big NFL punishment
away.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is back on the field after being out for three games with an injury, but he's already getting slapped with punishment from the NFL. According to a report from NBC Sports' Pro Football Talk , the NFL has officially fined Chicago's quarterback $23,882 for wearing an "unauthorized logo" on his shoes during the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots . That's two times the amount he was fined last week for wearing the shoes in Week 6, which was $11,941. But it appears Williams isn't sweating it. This week, he said that he'll still sport the shoes, which don't have an official deal with the NFL. Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams isn't backing down after another NFL fine "I try to be healthy. They're smart cleats," Williams said during a presser this week, per NBC Sports. "They're science cleats, and they've been working for me. A bunch of other guys wear them in the league, and they're forward-focused on making sure players stay on the field, and that's what I'm always focused on." Mike Florio says Williams "presumably will appeal the second fine." Plus, the NFL is expected to keep giving fines to Williams in increasing amounts until Williams gives in, Florio notes. "At some point, the league could (in theory) prevent Williams from playing in the non-conforming shoes," he adds. "Neither fine letter, however, warns him that he could be kept from playing with the Caddix shoes." Next up for the Bears, Williams and his cleats will take on the Seattle Seahawks for a "Monday Night Football" matchup on the road. Want more articles like this? away.headline: Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks
away.blurb: Ten players were listed as limited, though in the case of veteran outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence, it was for rest. home.headline: Seahawks Give New Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Before Bears Game
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks are getting closer to Zach Charbonnet's return, but head coach Mike Macdonald isn't ready to put a date on it. "He had a great week, great spirits," Macdonald said. "We have to remember, it's going to be nine months out of ACL surgery. How many people have ever done that? What's it like, Adrian Peterson?" Macdonald wasn't predicting a similar season for Charbonnet. Rather, his comments underscored the significance of attempting to return from major knee surgery on such an accelerated timeline. The roster move made him eligible to play, but Macdonald has repeatedly emphasized that his return will depend on the team's recovery plan. Charbonnet's eventual return would give Seattle another proven rushing option, particularly near the goal line. His absence has been especially noticeable with Kenneth Walker III now playing for the Chiefs and rookie Jadarian Price sidelined. Rookie Jadarian Price is expected to return to practice this week after missing multiple games with a chest injury.
